clinician.final_diagnosis: Autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease with right pelvic ectopic multicystic kidney
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 46-year-old Ghanaian male presented with painless total hematuria and left flank pain, with hypertension (BP 154/112 mmHg) on initial examination. Abdominal ultrasound revealed bilaterally enlarged kidneys with multiple cysts of varying sizes, with the right kidney ectopically located in the right iliac fossa. CT scan confirmed enlarged kidneys with renal parenchyma replaced by innumerable cysts of varying sizes, measuring 21×9.8 cm on the left and 18.8×8.0 cm for the ectopic right pelvic kidney. Laboratory evaluation revealed severe renal dysfunction (creatinine 518 μmol/l, eGFR 13 ml/min). Workup for hematuria including urine cytology and urethrocystoscopy ruled out malignancy. The combination of bilateral cystic renal disease with severe CKD and hypertension supported ADPKD affecting the left kidney, while the right kidney was identified as an ectopic multicystic kidney located in the pelvis.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Bilateral enlarged kidneys with multiple cysts consistent with polycystic kidney disease
Right kidney ectopically located in the right pelvis measuring 18.8×8.0 cm
Left kidney enlarged (21×9.8 cm) with innumerable cysts consistent with ADPKD
Severe chronic kidney disease (CKD stage 5) with eGFR 13 ml/min and creatinine 518 μmol/l
Hematuria workup negative for malignancy (urine cytology negative, cystoscopy normal)
Hypertension (154/112 mmHg) at presentation, consistent with ADPKD
